{{short description|Norwegian mathematician}}
[[File:Piene ragni.jpg|thumb|Ragni Piene]]

'''Ragni Piene''' (born 18 January 1947, [[Oslo]])<ref>[http://folk.uio.no/ragnip/RPieneCV_11.pdf CV] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910082538/http://folk.uio.no/ragnip/RPieneCV_11.pdf |date=2012-09-10 }}</ref> is a [[Norway|Norwegian]] [[mathematician]], specializing in [[algebraic geometry]], with particular interest in enumerative results and intersection theory.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mn.uio.no/math/english/people/aca/ragnip/rpienecv_2017.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|access-date=2018-05-01}}</ref>

==Education and career==
After a bachelor's degree from the [[University of Oslo]] in 1969 and a DEA from [[Université de Paris]] in 1970 <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://womeninmath.net/catalogue/|title=Ragni Piene - Women of Mathematics throughout Europe. A gallery of portraits|website=womeninmath.net/catalogue/|access-date=2021-05-14}}</ref> Piene received a doctorate in mathematics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1976, advised by [[Steven Kleiman]]. Her dissertation was titled ''Plücker Formulas''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=35972|title=Ragni Piene - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.ams.org|access-date=2018-05-01}}</ref>

She was appointed professor at the [[University of Oslo]] in 1987.<ref name="snl">{{cite encyclopedia|year=2007|title=Ragni Piene|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|editor=Henriksen, Petter|publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|location=Oslo|url=http://snl.no/Ragni_Piene|language=Norwegian|accessdate=29 October 2009}}</ref>

==Recognition==
She was elected a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] in 1994,<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|title=Gruppe 1: Matematiske fag|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=Norwegian|accessdate=29 October 2009|archive-date=17 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160317094243/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|url-status=dead}}</ref>
and in 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-05-05.</ref> and a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{citation|title=List of members|publisher=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members|accessdate=2020-10-02}}</ref> She is also one of the protagonists of the Women of mathematics exhibition. <ref>[https://womeninmath.net/protagonist/ragni-piene/ RAGNI PIENE - Women of Mathematics throughout Europe. A gallery of portraits]</ref>

==Service==
Since 2003 she has been a member of the executive committee of the [[International Mathematical Union]], and was the chair of the [[Abel Prize|Abel Committee]] from 2010–2011 to 2013–2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Abel Committee 2010/2011 |url=http://www.abelprize.no/c53678/artikkel/vis.html?tid=56493 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160509184830/http://www.abelprize.no/c53678/artikkel/vis.html?tid=56493 |archive-date=2016-05-09 |accessdate=4 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Abel Committee 2013/2014 |url=http://www.abelprize.no/c53678/artikkel/vis.html?tid=61675 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160509183200/http://www.abelprize.no/c53678/artikkel/vis.html?tid=61675 |archive-date=2016-05-09 |accessdate=4 January 2016}}</ref>
